purpose: A span waterfall: one row per span of a run (a function invocation, a request through several services), indented under the span it ran inside and drawn as a bar placed against the run's own clock. The rows form a tree grid that expands and collapses, a search narrows them to the spans whose name or service matches, and selecting a row opens its details (service, start, duration, share of the run, outcome message and attributes) under the waterfall. It reads a flat `spans` list with `parentId` links and never fetches anything.
useWhen: The test run of a function or the detail of one invocation, to show where the time went.
A request that crossed several services, each with its own span, where the order and the overlap matter.
Next to the run's logs (`log-view`), on the same clock.
avoidWhen: A list of log lines with levels → use `log-view`.
Durations to compare across many items with no parent/child relation → use `bar-list` or `chart`.
Status history of a service over days → use `tracker`.
related: log-view` — the run's log lines, shown under the trace on the same clock.
tree` — the same expand and collapse model without the time axis.
key-value-pairs` — the facts of the run above the trace.
bestPractices: Pass `start` and `duration` in milliseconds from the start of the run; the axis spans the latest end.
Link children with `parentId`; a span whose parent is missing becomes a root, so a partial trace still renders.
Set `status: 'error'` and a one-line `message` on the span that failed, and on its parents if the failure bubbled up.
Bind `v-model:selected` when another view (a request path, a log line) selects the same span.
Name the waterfall after the run (`aria-label="Trace of inv_7f21"`).
